The statistical second-law statement \\\\[ \\\\Sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}}[s,t] =I(X;R_s)-I(X;R_t) =I(X;R_s\\\\mid R_t)\\\\ge 0 \\\\] follows from data processing, but by itself it does not identify a physical energetic or thermodynamic cost. This paper establishes such a connection within an explicit and deliberately restricted stochastic-thermodynamic regime. We consider a finite observer memory $R_t$ coupled to a single heat bath at temperature $T$. A source label $X$ is fixed during the passive relaxation, the transition generator of $R_t$ is independent of $X$, and the memory dynamics satisfies detailed balance with respect to a strictly positive equilibrium law $q$. For the joint source--memory ensemble and for the unconditioned memory marginal, we define the standard stochastic-thermodynamic entropy-production rates. Using the relative-entropy chain rule and the detailed-balance $H$-theorem, we prove the exact correlation-dissipation decomposition \\\\[ \\\\frac{\\\\dot S_{\\\\mathrm{tot}}^{XR}}{k_B} = \\\\sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}} + \\\\frac{\\\\dot S_{\\\\mathrm{tot}}^{R}}{k_B}. \\\\] Consequently, \\\\[ \\\\dot S_{\\\\mathrm{tot}}^{XR}\\\\ge k_B\\\\sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}}, \\\\qquad \\\\Delta S_{\\\\mathrm{tot}}^{XR}[s,t]\\\\ge k_B\\\\Sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}}[s,t]. \\\\] At fixed temperature the same result is an excess-free-energy dissipation bound, \\\\[ \\\\Fex_{XR}(s)-\\\\Fex_{XR}(t) \\\\ge k_BT\\\\Sigma_{\\\\mathrm{obs}}[s,t]. \\\\] Equality holds when the memory marginal remains at equilibrium, in which case al…
